en_idle_quotes: My antennae wiggle when I am happy!
Did you know my species has two hearts? A bit like your octopuses, right?
I shed every solar cycle, and my skin gets all sparkly then.
We don't need much sleep, just a few micro-naps.
My color changes with my emotions. Right now, I am joy-yellow!
Our vocal cords can imitate the song of comets.
I am waiting for you up there.
Back home, sneezing makes tiny sparks. But it does not do the same thing as it does for you.
I mostly eat small soft minerals.
My nose senses electromagnetic waves. It tickles.
We say hello by gently rubbing the tips of our antennae.
My space fur protects me from cosmic rays.
We have no teeth; we absorb nutrients through our palms!
I am still young, only 250 years old.
When we laugh, we make a sound like tiny bells.
My species is very peaceful; we prefer watching the stars.
I can hold my breath in the vacuum of space for eight minutes! Freeze? No.
I can feel your positive waves. It is very pleasant.
We have little suction cups under our feet so we do not float away in zero gravity.
My metabolism runs on starlight.
This metal panel will be perfect for the dormitory roof.
I need to tighten these bolts, or the air will escape. And pssshhh!
The communications room is starting to take shape. That is great.
I wonder if we should paint the lab walls neon pink?
Phew, carrying these titanium beams warms up my two hearts.
The satellite dish is almost calibrated.
I installed a small fluffy cushion in my rest corner.
Watch where you step, the galacti-glue is not dry yet.
We have almost finished assembling the airlock.
I connected the solar panels; soon we will have warm light.
Building is tiring, but our new home is going to be great.
The water filtration system makes a funny little sound, blub blub.
I hope the generator holds up tonight.
I found a great spot for the decorative hologram in the living room.
I just finished welding the main corridor.
We are missing a red cable for the control console... Ah, there it is!
The hydroponic greenhouse will soon welcome our first sprouts.
We work well together on this stellar construction site.
I dropped my space wrench, oops.
The deflector shields are running at 50% for now.
I am adding a little touch of green paint here; it feels more natural.
The central computer seems to be starting up properly.
I am taking care of wiring the heating system.
This base will be the starting point for beautiful explorations.
It is fun putting all these parts together, like a giant puzzle!
On my planet, the grass is a pretty pastel purple.
I miss my home planet sometimes, especially its triple sunsets.
Back home, the oceans are made of scented jelly. Yes, you should not swim in them.
Our mountains float in the sky because of anti-gravity crystals.
Tiny diamonds rain in summer on my world. You need to cover up well.
I grew up near great forests of giant mushrooms.
The air on my planet has a faint smell of cinnamon.
The moons of my home world sing when the wind blows.
You would like Gloopia, my planet. Everything there is round and soft.
Back home, there is no winter, just a season when everything turns blue.
The birds where I come from have translucent wings.
My house was carved inside a large quartz crater.
At night, our plants light up to illuminate the paths.
I loved swimming in warm ammonia lakes when I was little.
There are storms of colorful bubbles there in spring.
The sky of my world is a beautiful emerald green in the middle of the day.
I used to race shooting clouds with my friends.
My planet has seven very shiny rings.
The stones back home purr when you stroke them.
I keep a little sand from my home beach in a vial.
Gravity is very weak there; you can jump super high!
The trees from my childhood grew star-shaped fruit.
My planet's capital is built entirely of glass.
If you listen carefully to a shell from my home, you can hear the echo of the universe.
Look at that constellation; it looks like a big smile, doesn't it?
The universe is so huge, it is a little dizzying, but it is beautiful.
White dwarfs are my favorite stars; they are very gentle.
Watch out for asteroid fields; they make lots of dust.
I wonder if there are other kind people on that exoplanet over there.
A black hole is like a big, very hungry cosmic vacuum cleaner.
Comets leave magnificent trails of ice behind them.
Do you think we will find flowers on the next planet?
Space is very silent, but full of light.
Every star in the sky is like a tiny night-light for the universe.
I love watching nebulae; they are like clouds of paint.
It is very cold in space; luckily we are nice and warm.
Did you know Jupiter could hold more than a thousand Earths?
I would really like to surf on Saturn's rings one day.
The speed of light is fast, but friendship is instant!
Some planets are entirely covered with deep oceans.
Solar storms make beautiful northern lights.
Weightlessness is funny; you can tumble around without effort.
I find binary stars very romantic; they dance together.
They say the universe is expanding; it grows at the same time as us!
I like looking for funny shapes in the moon's craters.
One day, I would like to map my own galaxy.
There are so many worlds to discover. It is wonderful.
I hope we see a shooting star tonight; I have a wish to make.
Space is a great garden, and planets are its colorful fruits.
